questions.question: When you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Wear your seat belt.
Limit your driving to weekdays.
Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Limit your driving to 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. What should you do to merge safely?

options.text: Use your side and rearview mirrors and check your blind spots.
Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Yield to traffic already on the freeway.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and yield to cars already on the freeway. Check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure you have space to merge safely.

questions.question: When driving in a travel lane:

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to look up an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance ramp.
Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never stop. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Do not stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull off the road. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or find a safe place to turn around.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol.
Amphetamines.
Anger.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol affect your driving ability in the same way. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours has the same effect as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: A person's driving ability can be impaired by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Any medication.
Lack of sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving depends on being in good physical condition. Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness can all impair your driving ability.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic from the right.
Highway curves ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is merging into your lane from the right.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Divided highway ends.
Two-way traffic.
Keep left.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Call the police immediately.
Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.
Do something aggressive back at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get even with an aggressive driver makes the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of them.
Stop to let them cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians and other cars that may be in the intersection, even if you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Stay away from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, move away from them. Don't look at them or make gestures that could upset them more. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever keeps you safe.

questions.question: Night driving is harder than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat faster at night.
You can't see as well in the dark.
It rains more often at night.
You meet more motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can't see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can't see as far. Use your headlights and drive slow enough to stop within the distance you can see ahead.

questions.question: When driving on wet roads, remember:

options.text: Roads are most slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra space when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are slippery, especially right after rain starts. Your tires lose grip on the layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down during heavy rain or when water is on the road.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry about it because all cars are the same.
Not tell your friend you don't know the car.
Ignore any problems so you don't embarrass your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, find the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn. Check for any problems and fix them before you drive.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other cars are doing instead.
Assume the flagger shouldn't be there.
Follow the normal road rules.

questions.explanation: When a flagger directs traffic, you must obey them. Ignoring them is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Check your mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to see your blind spot.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
A stop sign is present.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to, if there's a stop sign, or if red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep looking around.
Be ready to react to hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways so you can react to surprises. Don't stare at one spot for too long to avoid highway hypnosis.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should let drivers on the public road go first.
Can force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will move for them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should let drivers on the public road go first.
questions.explanation: If you're entering traffic from a driveway or private road, let drivers on the public road pass first. Merge safely when you have an opening.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The sidewalk width.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are entitled to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign tells you that people may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: The best way to avoid hydroplaning is to:

options.text: Keep your tires properly maintained.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Watch out for standing water or puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car needs more distance to stop and may skid during quick turns. Do not use cruise control when driving in wet or icy conditions. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you're driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain makes it hard to see, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If the rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull off the road and stop until it lets up.

questions.question: When parents or guardians sign the consent form for their teenage child's learner license, they are saying that:

options.text: Their child has passed a driver education course.
Their child is a careful driver.
Their child's listed date of birth is correct.
They accept financial responsibility for any damage caused by the minor while operating a motor vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They accept financial responsibility for any damage caused by the minor while operating a motor vehicle.
questions.explanation: A parent or guardian must sign a consent form for a teenager under 18 to get a learner license. By signing, they agree to pay for any damage caused by the teenager while driving.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
The road ahead has a series of turns or curves.
Traffic increases ahead.
Steep grade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the pavement is slippery when wet. In wet conditions, reduce your speed, avoid braking or turning suddenly, and stay farther away from the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: A minor traffic safety problem.
A serious traffic safety problem.
Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while drunk or impaired is a serious traffic safety problem. Safe driving is impossible when you drink alcohol or use other drugs. Drunk driving endangers you and everyone else on the road.

questions.question: When you approach a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop. Running a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on a steady red light only if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the pavement.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your vehicle's speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the pavement.

questions.question: While driving, you must stop your vehicle:

options.text: At an intersection with a stop sign.
At a red light.
When a traffic officer orders you to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop and check for pedestrians and cross traffic. Wait until the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing the radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions every mile. You need to focus all your attention on driving. Any extra task can be dangerous.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Let it go.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut off the other driver to get back at them.

questions.explanation: Do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Let it go and keep driving safely. This prevents road rage and danger.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, or turn around on the highway. Do not cross the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.
